summary: This first-day Paradiso workshop extends the existing Dante cluster by making imagination the road past exam logic, poetry a literal-and-metaphorical access surface, free will a soul/body struggle under fear, and forgiveness the outside grace that can interrupt self-made hell.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Dante cannot be entered by clever AP-style logic alone; intuition, imagination, paradox, ambiguity, and memory-breaking poetic compression are the route toward Paradise.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Poetry already carries the June 15 Paradiso method layer. This source gives the fuller workshop origin for imagination as true-truth access, poetry as literal and metaphorical at once, and memory as inadequate to the vision.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Writing Paradise in Tuscan and making a common man the center of sacred literature becomes a rebellion over access and a launch point for modern individuality.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The Poetry page already distinguishes Dante's access revolution from institutional mediation. This source adds the strong Paradise-side version: theology explains religion, but poetry activates religious imagination.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Paradise begins by making heaven and hell necessary for real choice, then uses Piccarda to show how fear-shaped desire can make a lower station feel proper.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Free Will already carries chosen hell and the June 15 Piccarda layer. This source intensifies it with the full Cantos 1-5 workshop argument that if the will exists, a path opens, and a soul's place cannot be treated as mere external assignment.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Piccarda's worldview turns agency into defiance and obedience into piety, so her failure of will becomes a programming trap rather than only an external abduction.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The source gives a positive Dante counterform to obedience-renamed-freedom: absolute will belongs to the soul, contingent will to the frightened body, and love/knowledge are remedies for divided will.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Broken vows deform trust, identity, and agency; the impossible repair comes when forgiveness from outside the self interrupts the worldview that the sinner already deserves.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Human Heart already carries promise/forgiveness/fallibility. This source adds the vow-as-trust and hell-as-not-forgiving-yourself route, while Free Will keeps the agency mechanics.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The workshop is framed as life-transforming Great Books practice, and Jiang closes by telling students to trust intuition and imagination, challenge him, and make the classroom a Paradise-like surface of questioning.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Dead World owns the escape from school/material/exam logic. Living School receives bounded classroom-method pressure, but the active mechanism here is Great Books as an imagination-training escape practice.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use this 2026-06-17 first-day workshop when Poetry next receives Dante replacement/compression: Paradise starts from imagination before analysis, defines poetry as literal and metaphorical at once, uses Apollo/pagan memory to reach Christian heaven, and makes vernacular Dante a common-person revolution that activates religious imagination.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Poetry owns access, language, memory, and civilizational transmission. Free Will owns the will under fear; Human Heart owns forgiveness and trust; Dead World owns escape from dead school logic.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold for a future Free Will compression: Piccarda's coerced vow becomes Jiang's strongest Paradiso case for fear splitting will into soul and body, with absolute will remaining faithful while contingent will yields to bodily danger, rationalization, and a worldview of helpless obedience.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: This remains Free Will rather than Taboo or Religion As Administrative Filter because the active mechanism is agency under coercion and fear, not ritual boundary or priestly office.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use as sequel pressure to the June 16-17 heart layer: a vow is spoken trust, not private bookkeeping; betrayal changes self-understanding; the repair question becomes whether unconditional forgiveness can reach a person who cannot forgive himself.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Human Heart owns trust, forgiveness, and relation repair. Free Will owns the soul/body will model and Piccarda's chosen station; Poetry owns the Dante method making the moral frame available.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use only in a future Great Books escape-practice compression: Jiang frames the workshop as life-transforming wisdom and repeatedly distinguishes imagination, intuition, debate, and direct reading from AP-style logic and dead school habits.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Dead World owns escape from dead ontology and school logic. Education owns ordinary school formation; Living School owns the institutional/classroom method only as a bounded secondary route.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use only as public-classroom method pressure: the livestream makes real-time questions, open challenge, exact text, and debate part of the learning surface, but it is not primarily an institution-building source.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Living School should not absorb the Dante concept. It gets the classroom scene only when the public-school method itself is being compared.

new_lens_seeds.title: Paradise Begins Where Logic Fails
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Some worlds cannot be entered by detached cleverness. Paradise demands imagination, intuition, paradox, ambiguity, memory failure, and direct participation before it can be understood.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: This mechanism can organize the first-day Paradiso workshop and compare Great Books, poetry, dead school logic, religious imagination, and reader transformation, but it is still better routed through existing Poetry and Dead World surfaces until more non-Dante sources require a separate page.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as a seed only. Do not create standalone Paradiso, Paradise, Dante Workshop, Imagination Before Logic, or Paradise Begins Where Logic Fails pages from this source alone.

new_lens_seeds.title: Fear Makes Will Contingent
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: The soul may want God, but the frightened body yields to threat, survival, and rationalization; the yielded act then becomes a worldview that makes agency feel like defiance or impossibility.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The Piccarda case names a reusable agency-under-coercion mechanism relevant to school, church, state, and family, but current Free Will anchors already carry chosen hell, obedience renamed freedom, and anti-love denial of agency.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as a seed. Do not create standalone Piccarda, Absolute Will, Contingent Will, Fear Makes Will Contingent, Coerced Vow, or Agency Under Coercion pages from this source alone.

new_lens_seeds.title: Vow-Breaking Destroys Agency
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: A vow becomes real through spoken trust; breaking it does not merely violate a rule but changes self-understanding, invites rationalization, and can trap the person in a fate he thinks he deserves until forgiveness arrives from outside.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The mechanism can compare marriage, covenant, promise-making, institutional vow, self-forgiveness, and divine grace, but Human Heart and Free Will already have active homes for trust repair and agency.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as a seed. Do not create standalone Vow, Covenant, Cheating, Betrayal, Vow-Breaking Destroys Agency, or Self-Forgiveness pages from this source alone.

new_lens_seeds.title: Body-Cosmos As Intentional Order
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Dante's body metaphor lets Jiang reject a purely emergent universe: distance, hierarchy, spheres, and divine powers are narrated as parts of an intentional living order rather than dead mechanism.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The body-cosmos sequence may later help Dead World, Sacred Machines, Poetry, and Free Will compare living cosmology against materialist reduction, but this single workshop does not yet require a public concept.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as a seed. Do not create standalone Body-Cosmos, Dante Cosmology, Spheres, Medieval Science, Moon Science, Intentional Universe, or Living Cosmos pages from this source alone.

chronology_notes.note: Although processed after earlier June 15-17 Paradiso records, this source is the newly published first-day Dante workshop on Cantos 1-5, dated 2026-06-17. Treat it as a dense foundational Paradiso source, not as a separate public Dante surface.

This source strengthens the Paradiso method chronology: June 15 already carried imagination/paradox against school logic, while this full workshop adds poetry as literal-and-metaphorical simultaneity, Apollo/pagan memory, vernacular rebellion, and poetry activating religious imagination.

This source gives the full Piccarda agency layer behind later compact Paradiso references: absolute will, contingent bodily fear, rationalization, and a worldview of helpless obedience must be kept distinct from generic victimhood or simple institutional critique.

The source comes after the June 16 promise-making layer and before/alongside the June 17 forgiveness-as-imagination layer: it makes the intermediate trust sequence explicit, from public vow to self-deformation to the need for forgiveness from outside the trapped self.
